title: Sunny Lands and Seas
subtitle: A Voyage in the SS. ‘Ceylon.’ Notes Made during a Five Months’ Tour in India—the Straits Settlements—Manila—China—Japan—the Sandwich Islands—and California

summary: Hugh Wilkinson, a London barrister, was one of the passengers of the SS. Ceylon, a steamer that took a party of travellers round the world as an “ocean-yachting” cruise in 1881–82. The book is made of his letters from the five months of the voyage: by Egypt and the Suez Canal to Bombay; across northern India by Jeypore, Delhi, Agra, Lucknow, and Benares to Calcutta; to the Straits Settlements, Manila, Hong Kong, and Canton; through Japan, from Nagasaki and Kioto to Yokohama; across the Pacific to the Sandwich Islands; and to California and the Yosemite Valley. Japan takes about seventy pages, among them a chapter on an account of a hara-kiri. It has about forty wood engravings and a map of the route.
